'''Rashna Bhandari''' is head, Laboratory of Cell Signalling at the [[Centre for DNA Fingerprinting and Diagnostics]], Hyderabad. Bhandari is pursuing her study on signal transduction in biological systems, with particular emphasis on understanding the role of inositol pyrophosphates in physiology and metabolism.

==Education==
Bhandari obtained her bachelor's degree in human biology from the [[All India Institute of Medical Sciences]], followed by post graduation and doctorate in biological sciences from the [[Indian Institute of Science]].<ref name="Profile">{{cite web|title=CDFD Profile - Rashna Bhandari|url=http://www.cdfd.org.in/labpages/dr_rashna_bhandari.html|accessdate=16 July 2016|archive-date=11 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170611152101/http://www.cdfd.org.in/labpages/dr_rashna_bhandari.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Career==
Bhandari joined [[Centre for DNA Fingerprinting and Diagnostics]] in 2008 as a staff scientist.

Post her doctorate at [[Indian Institute of Science]], Bhandari worked with [[Sandhya Srikant Visweswariah]] on signal transduction by the membrane-bound guanylyl cyclase, GCC, which is involved in maintaining fluid and ion homeostasis across the intestinal membrane.<ref name="WellcomeBT">{{cite web|title=Fellow Profile |url=http://www.wellcomedbt.org/fellowsprofile/dr-rashna-bhandari-96|accessdate=16 July 2016}}</ref>

In 2001, Bhandari joined [[John Kuriyan]] laboratory at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] as a post-doctoral fellow to work on the [[structural biology]] and [[biochemistry]] of proteins involved in [[cell signaling]].<ref name="WellcomeBT"/>
In 2003, Bhandari relocated to the [[Johns Hopkins School of Medicine]] in Baltimore, where she worked with [[Solomon H. Snyder|Solomon Snyder]] on deciphering the role of inositol pyrophosphates as signalling molecules.<ref name="WellcomeBT"/>

In 2015, a group led by Bhandari found that mice with lower levels of IP7 show reduced blood clotting.  Inadequate levels of IP7 led to reduction in another phosphate-rich molecule called polyphosphate (a long chain of phosphate groups linked to each other). In mammals, polyphosphate is predominantly found in platelets and helps in strengthening blood clots during their formation. Polyphosphates housed inside platelets break up during clotting. These polyphosphates and other components get released to form a mesh that constitutes the basic structure for clot. Lowering IP7 levels could have potential applications in the prevention of stroke or myocardial infarction by reducing clotting.<ref name="Hindu">{{cite news|title=Small molecule with a huge potential|url=https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/science/small-molecule-with-a-huge-potential/article6909412.ece|date=18 February 2015|first=Y.|last=Mallikarjun|newspaper=The Hindu|access-date=21 June 2018}}</ref>

Bhandari believes that ambition leads to success and not gender.<ref name="NewIndiaExpress">{{cite web|title=In media |url=http://www.newindianexpress.com/states/andhra_pradesh/article255835.ece|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160816220112/http://www.newindianexpress.com/states/andhra_pradesh/article255835.ece|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 August 2016|accessdate=16 July 2016}}</ref>
